source: hand-authored fixture for issue #211 — not shipped data
description: The healthy counterpart of drug-reference-name-not-its-own-alias.json: the same three ibuprofen rows, authored the way the shipped datasets are. Two differences, and BOTH are needed — measured, because declaring substanceName alone is not enough. (1) Each row declares `substanceName`, the reference data's own claim that these rows are one substance. (2) The presentations are named with a TRAILING PARENTHESIZED qualifier, which is the convention DrugReference.substanceKey is built around (`Dexamethasone (nasal)`) — a curated file publishes no substance registry, so the display STEM is the veto on that claim, and `Ibuprofen tablets` stems to itself while `Ibuprofen (tablets)` stems to `Ibuprofen`. Each row also lists its own display name among its aliases, as the ddinter and atc parsers do, so the loader has nothing to repair. Result: one substance, so the per-substance verdict keeps every rule-bearing row, and the validity check reports nothing at all.
